1.explanation:
• lib/modeling/cmd/SetColorHandler.js: This handler applies both fillColor and strokeColor to selected elements. It doesn’t distinguish external label shapes, so it applies the fill color to their text DI. Adjustments here are needed to detect external labels and apply strokeColor instead.  
• lib/modeling/BpmnUpdater.js: Responsible for persisting color changes into the BPMN DI. It currently writes fillColor for label text elements uniformly. It needs logic to write strokeColor for external labels.  
• lib/draw/BpmnRenderer.js: In its drawLabel() routine it picks up style.fill for rendering label text. External labels should be rendered using style.stroke. This file requires a conditional branch for external labels.  
• lib/draw/BpmnRenderUtil.js: Extracts shape style from DI and maps fillColor→fill and strokeColor→stroke. For external labels the mapping of strokeColor should drive the text fill style. The style computation must be updated accordingly.  
• lib/draw/TextRenderer.js: Always uses the computed style.fill for the <text> element’s fill attribute. It needs to fall back to style.stroke when rendering external labels.  
• lib/util/LabelUtil.js: Contains utilities to detect whether a shape is an external label. This helper is needed in the above modules to conditionally apply strokeColor instead of fillColor when rendering and updating external label text.
1.bug_scenario: When the user invokes modeling.setColor on an external label shape, the label’s text is being rendered in the “fill” color (a very light shade) instead of the “stroke” color (the darker border color). Embedded labels continue to use the stroke color for their text, so this inconsistent behavior on external labels leads to poor text readability.

2.explanation:
• lib/features/modeling/cmd/SetColorHandler.js is the command handler for modeling.setColor and is responsible for writing both fill and stroke attributes onto the SVG elements. It doesn’t special-case external labels, and so applies fillColor to text nodes where it should apply strokeColor.  
• lib/features/modeling/BpmnUpdater.js persists the color changes into the BPMN DI model. It currently handles stroke/fill on shapes but does not distinguish label elements, so DI updates for label strokes may also be missing or inverted.  
• lib/draw/TextRenderer.js is used by the renderer to actually create and update <text> elements. By default it sets text ‘fill’ attributes; it needs to map the stroke color into the text fill for external labels.  
• lib/draw/BpmnRenderer.js sits on top of TextRenderer and contains the logic to render embedded vs. external labels. It must be taught to use strokeColor (not fillColor) when rendering label text outside of shapes.  
• lib/draw/BpmnRenderUtil.js defines the default style constants for labels (e.g. using fillColor by default). The external-label style there should be adjusted to reference stroke color so that setColor consistently uses the darker stroke color for all labels.
2.bug_scenario: When you select an external label (e.g. the “foo” or “bar” text under a circle) and call modeling.setColor on that label, the label’s text is being colored with the “fill” color (a very light yellow) instead of the “stroke” color (the darker orange). Embedded labels (text inside a shape) correctly pick up the stroke color, but external labels do not – leading to poor contrast in the UI.
